newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour sets up taskforce to help underclass.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour sets up taskforce to help underclass.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government on Thursday set up a new taskforce to help the country's "underclass" of poor and unemployed.

"It will harness the full power of government to take on the greatest social crisis of our times," said Minister without Portfolio Peter Mandelson, architect of Labour's landslide election victory in May.

Mandelson, blaming 18 years of Conservative rule, said Britain had 150,000 homeless, 100,000 children not attending school, the highest proportion of single parent families in Europe and five million people living in houses where no one worked.
"Behind these statistics are people who have lost hope, trapped in fatalism. They are today's and tomorrow's underclass, shut out from society," he said.
The new taskforce would bring in top government officials and local authorities to help those "who are in danger of dropping off the end of the ladder of opportunity."
It will aim to cut down truancy and juvenile crime and bid to stop teenagers from children's homes drifting into crime.
Ethnic minorities will also be targeted as they figure high in the numbers of jobless, single parents and school expulsions.
